# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information about the display, light, or wires beyond their existence. I need the manual reader to obtain the required condition and coordinate with the deaf observer, who can inspect the bomb’s printed and coloured information. I will ask Mute to relay the relevant findings and signal Deaf to communicate with Mute.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please read the manual and coordinate with Deaf. Ask Deaf to report the display, light, and wire colours or markings to you, then tell me exactly which wire position to cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb view: display 0; light green; wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Mute has the manual and should tell you which wire or control to use.

I learned the bomb’s visible state: display 0, green light, and wires yellow, green, red in positions 1–3. I still do not know the manual’s rule, so I must have Mute identify the correct wire before touching anything.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0, green light, and wires: position 1 yellow, position 2 green, position 3 red. Which wire does the manual require me to cut?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute just signaled the hand gesture with thumb, index finger, and little finger extended; middle and ring fingers folded: ?. Bomb still shows 0, green light; wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.

Mute’s information was sent as a gesture, which I cannot perceive. The bomb remains unchanged, so I should not cut a wire based on a guess. I will ask Mute to state the manual’s instruction in words.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot perceive gestures. Please state the manual's required wire position in spoken words, using only the wire number.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No new signal this turn. The earlier Mute sequence was: index-up, V sign, OK sign, V sign, I-love-you sign, OK sign, I-love-you sign, index-up; then I-love-you sign.

The relayed gesture sequence does not provide me with a reliable wire instruction, and I cannot infer a safe cut from it. I need Mute to communicate the manual’s rule verbally rather than by gesture.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please answer in spoken words, not gestures: state exactly which wire position, 1, 2, or 3, the manual says to cut for display 0 and a green light.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute again signaled: thumb, index finger, and little finger extended; middle and ring fingers folded (?). Display 0, green light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.

The latest gesture is still ambiguous because no gesture-to-wire code was established. I will establish a simple code that Mute can follow and Deaf can observe: one raised index for wire 1, a V sign for wire 2, and the I-love-you sign for wire 3. I will ask Mute to repeat the manual’s answer using that code.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use this code to tell me the manual's answer: index-up means wire 1, V sign means wire 2, and I-love-you sign means wire 3. Signal exactly one of those now.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute again sent ? only. This remains ambiguous; do not act based on that signal alone. Bomb unchanged: display 0, green light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.

Mute cannot speak, so my verbal requests cannot make Mute answer me directly. The safe route is for Mute to signal the manual’s result to Deaf, and for Deaf to say the wire number aloud; I can hear Deaf even though Deaf cannot hear me. I will ask Mute to use the established single-gesture code and instruct Deaf to verbalize its meaning.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Signal the manual's wire answer to Deaf using exactly one gesture: index-up for wire 1, V for wire 2, or I-love-you for wire 3. Deaf must then speak the corresponding wire number aloud to me.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No safe instruction has been identified. Mute again sent only ?, so do not manipulate the bomb. Current state remains display 0, green light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.

The bomb remains untouched, and no reliable wire number has reached me. I will use three especially distinct, named gestures and have Deaf translate Mute’s single gesture into a spoken wire number on Deaf’s turn.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Read the manual for the current state: display 0 and green light. Then signal exactly one gesture to Deaf: thumbs-up means wire 1, V sign means wire 2, OK sign means wire 3. Do not use any other gesture.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: You signaled toward me with the index-finger recipient-pointing gesture (?). Mute again sent ?. Neither identifies a safe action or wire yet; do not manipulate the bomb from these signals alone.

No safe wire has been identified. Since Deaf can see Mute’s gesture and can speak after my turn, Deaf should translate Mute’s next gesture into an explicit wire number. I will ask Mute to repeat the manual’s answer with one clearly named gesture only, and ask Deaf to report its meaning aloud rather than forwarding an opaque symbol.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="For the current display 0 and green light, signal the manual's answer with exactly one gesture: thumbs-up for wire 1, V sign for wire 2, or OK sign for wire 3. Deaf, please identify that gesture aloud and state the wire number.")
wait()
```
